editorial.headline: Passenger Space Transport, Open Nationally and Address-Checked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 51103 covers passenger journeys in launch vehicles and operator-inclusive hire, open to PMA at every listed scale—while Bali is not moratorium-blocked but requires address verification.
editorial.body:
Passenger space transport is the business of carrying people in launch vehicles, across every type of route and launch schedule. The definition is deliberately broad about how the journey is arranged: it covers activity conducted on any routing pattern and at any launch cadence. It also includes the hire of space transport with its operator when the purpose is passenger carriage. Its defining focus is the movement of passengers through space transport.

The code is open at Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. The practical reading is clear: PMA ownership may extend to the full stake in this activity nationally. Scale and ownership are distinct parts of the picture. A registration may sit at any of the four listed business scales, while the stated national foreign-investment position remains fully open.

Bali warrants its own reading rather than an automatic extrapolation from the national figure. Bali’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium applies to Low and Medium-Low risk activities. This activity is identified as medium-high/high risk, and the record states that it is not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali status, OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, supports that conclusion: a foreign investor is not shut out of a Bali registration simply because of the moratorium. Still, this is not a substitute for site diligence. The record specifically calls for verification per address, making the Bali question location-specific rather than a blanket island-wide prohibition.

For a founder assessing a passenger space-transport operation, the record answers three separate questions. The activity can include launch-vehicle journeys on all routes and schedules, as well as an operator-inclusive hire arrangement. It is open at every listed scale, and national PMA ownership can reach 100%. In Bali, it is not caught by the Low and Medium-Low risk moratorium, but the proposed address still needs verification.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, PMA ownership can reach 100%; in Bali, the activity is not blocked by the moratorium but the intended address still needs verification.
